title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. In each phase two blocks at the left end grow by eating a long run of ones (one double cycle proved in Lean). A plain simulation, run in checked pieces, finds no halt in 1.08·1013 steps, and the fixed block accelerator none in 1.417·1013. The run alternates phases that turn the left zone (100)^a into a block of 5-cell words with phases that regrow it. An irregular stretch (up to about 1.3 million cells) is built at the hand-overs and eaten later; it is not understood. A halt needs a 1 read in state C next to a long run of ones. (An earlier accelerated run reported larger bounds and a halt at 6.38·1013; both came from a bug, now fixed.)

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 0 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 45,689 cells have been visited and 21,011 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The plain C simulator c/snap.c runs 5·1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the tape spans cells −1,125,275 to 24,097.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.083·10<sup>13</sup> steps (plain simulation in pieces)
claims.text: A plain simulator that starts from a saved tape (c/plainfrom.c) runs each stretch between consecutive kept checkpoints of the fixed accelerated run, from the plain tape at 5·1011 to 1.083·1013 steps (47 stretches). Each ends with the same tape, head and state as the next checkpoint, and none halts, so together they are a plain run of the first 1.083·1013 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.417·10<sup>13</sup> steps (fixed accelerated run)
claims.text: The block accelerator c/bacc.cpp (whole-block crossings, repeated moving fronts, cached 64-cell chunks), with the chunk bug fixed on 25 November 2026, runs from the plain simulator's tape at 5·1011 steps to 1.417·1013 without a halt. An earlier run of the unfixed tool reported bounds up to 1.9·1013 and a halt at 6.38·1013; it went wrong at about 2.13·1012, and those results are withdrawn.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.464). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: In periodic notation the tape at 109 steps is (100)^6706 1 D>0 (101)^468 10 (011)^2 (01)^4857 (101)^3 (01)^2 (101)^3 (01)^2 ...: a long block (100)^n at the growing left end, then blocks of (101) and (01) that the head converts, and further right a long periodic region of (101)^3 (01)^2 units. At 108 steps the left block was (100)^2053.

claims.title: The growth phase
claims.text: 0^inf B> 0 (011)^(n+2) 0 011 011 (01)^(m+1) (01101)^(q+1) 011 111 R reaches 0^inf B> 0 (011)^(n+3) 0 011 011 (01)^(m+4) (01101)^(q+1) 011 R (written as the run re-brackets it) in 10m+20n+20q+204 steps, for all n, m, q and every tape R.

claims.title: Phases
claims.text: The run alternates growth phases, in which the blocks (011)^n and (01)^m at the left end grow by eating a long run of ones three cells per double cycle, with an irregular stretch in which the head works through a list of short words; the runs of ones are made by earlier phases.

claims.title: Two kinds of phase, to 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: Seen from far away the tape is (100)^a, then a run of ones or a block of (011), then a block of 5-cell words (rotations of 00111 or 01011), then an irregular stretch. The run alternates phases with the left end fixed, in which (100)^a is turned into 5-words, and phases with the left end moving, in which (100)^a grows by eating ones. Since 2.8·10<sup>11</sup> steps the 66,518 5-words and the 120,574-cell irregular stretch have not changed; that phase ends when a run of ones further right (54,641 cells at 5·10<sup>11</sup>) is used up.

claims.title: Phases past 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The regular phase ends at about 5.95·10<sup>11</sup> steps. A hand-over then eats part of the irregular stretch and rebuilds the tape (about 9.2·10<sup>11</sup>). A longer regular phase follows (to 1.86·10<sup>12</sup>), and then a second hand-over in which the irregular stretch grows to about 880,000 cells (2.16·10<sup>12</sup>). The hand-overs, the only places a halt could come from so far, are not decoded. In the fixed run the left zone has become 385,143 five-cell words by about 3.7·10<sup>12</sup>; it then grows back (to about 842,000 copies) while the 5-word block is eaten, a third hand-over (8.1 to 9.3·10<sup>12</sup>) builds an irregular stretch of about 1.3 million cells, and from 1.08·10<sup>13</sup> the left zone is again turned into a 5-word block (about 638,000 words at 1.417·10<sup>13</sup>). Each cycle is two to three times the size of the one before.

claims.title: Two pumps, in run lengths
claims.text: At the visits of the left end in state D the tape is 1 2^a FRONT ... X ... (run lengths). Two regimes alternate: 3 2^2 1^k at the front (two visits: a+1, k+3, X-3) and (1 2)^j at the front (one visit: a+2, j-1, X-3); in both a single long run X further right loses 3 cells. When X reaches 0 a stretch of the irregular list behind it is rewritten at once; those rewrites are not decoded.

claims.title: No acceleration found
claims.text: An exact macro simulator with blocks of 2, 3, 6 or 12 cells and linear cycle jumps agrees with the plain machine but does not get past plain speed: the tape mixes words of period 2, 3 and 5 cells and has tens of thousands of runs of blocks (24,000 at 5·10<sup>10</sup> steps).

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 16, history 1 up to width 15, history 2 up to width 13, history 3 up to width 12, LRU history up to width 4 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 12, p = 3 up to width 12, p = 4 up to width 12, p = 6 up to width 12. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in the 47 of 120 parameter sets that were run (sweep not finished). Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..9; n = 10 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: the rule for the irregular region between phases; see Next steps in the README.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1RE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 45,689 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks that grow by eating runs of ones
html: At the moments the head is at the left end in state B, the tape often reads

Two blocks, (011)^n and (01)^m, then a middle block, then a long run of ones. Every two cycles the run of ones loses three cells and the blocks grow: n goes up by one and m by three. This is proved in Lean for all sizes.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 70' role='img' aria-label='two blocks at the left, a middle block, and a run of ones being eaten' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='15' width='120' height='24' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='70' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(011)^n</text><rect x='130' y='15' width='140' height='24' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='200' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(01)^m</text><rect x='270' y='15' width='100' height='24' fill='var(--sunk)' stroke='var(--line-strong)'/><text x='320' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>(01101)^q</text><rect x='370' y='15' width='170' height='24' fill='none' stroke='var(--head)'/><text x='455' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>1^r: eaten 3 at a time</text></svg>

When the run of ones is gone, the head works through an irregular list of short words further right, and later a new phase starts with the next long run of ones. That irregular part is not understood, so there is no rule from one phase to the next.

Where it could halt

Only in state C on a 1 with at least six 1s to its left: next to a long run of ones, the very thing the phases eat. Inside a phase this never happens; it would have to happen in the irregular part.

sections.heading: Two pumps that empty a long run three cells at a time
html: Write the tape as the lengths of its runs of 1s. At the visits of the left end it reads 1 2^a FRONT ... X ...: a growing block of runs of 2, a short front, and somewhere further right a single long run X. Two regimes alternate:

In both, the head runs out to the long run, takes three cells from it and brings them back to the growing blocks. When the run is empty the head rewrites a stretch of the list behind it in one long excursion, and a new long run appears elsewhere. That list is long and irregular (about 4,000 runs after 2·108 steps), and the rule of these rewrites has not been found; this is what keeps the machine open, and also what makes it slow to simulate: none of the accelerated simulators used for its neighbours gets past plain speed here.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.464). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,689 cells (25,401 left of the start, 4,417 right), with a density of 1s of 0.46.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Two blocks (011)^n (01)^m at the left end grow by pumping three cells at a time out of a long run of ones further right (proved in Lean); when the run is used up a long irregular list of short words is rewritten, and that part is not decoded; no macro simulator tried accelerates it; open.
family: growing blocks pumping cells out of long runs, irregular list behind
